title: Dry-fit two loose boards end to end on three dowels: all three into their holes at once, seam closed and flush
instruction: Two loose boards lie flat on the bench, end to end along y, 0.51 m apart. Three hardwood dowels stand 20 mm out of the end of the dark board on the right; the pale board on the left has three matching round holes in its end. Join them in a dry fit: bring the boards together so all three dowels go into their holes, push the joint closed until the two ends meet along the whole seam, with the boards level with each other and their edges flush, then let go of both.
context: Carpenters (O*NET 47-2031, Employment 2025: 889,700) have the Core task "Assemble and fasten materials to make frameworks or props, using hand tools and wood screws, nails, dowel pins, or glue."; cabinetmakers (51-7011, 81,800): "Attach parts or subassemblies together to form completed units, using glue, dowels, nails, screws, or clamps." A dowelling jig's manual ends each joint with "Test fit the joint.": the dry fit before glue. Three 8 mm dowels must enter three holes together; a board turned a few degrees or off to one side stops on the dowels' chamfers. Each board starts within reach of one arm only.
setup: Coordinates: x forward from the arm bases (at y +-0.305), y left, z up from the table top. Two loose boards lie flat on the bare bench, long axes along y: 150 x 70 x 19 mm, 0.135 kg each, wood friction 0.4 static / 0.35 dynamic. Pale hole board (sRGB (0.86, 0.74, 0.54)) centred at (0.35, 0.33), yaw 0; three 8 mm round holes 22 mm deep in its -y end. Dark dowel board (sRGB (0.36, 0.24, 0.16)) centred at (0.35, -0.33) shifted along x and turned by seed (seed mod 3 = 0: x 0 mm, yaw 0 deg; seed mod 3 = 1: x 12 mm, yaw 3 deg; seed mod 3 = 2: x -12 mm, yaw -3 deg); three fluted hardwood dowels, 8 mm x 40 mm, half in its +y end, 20 mm standing out, tips chamfered 1 mm x 45 deg. Dowels and holes 24 mm apart across the board, at mid-thickness. The two ends start 510 mm apart. In the sim each hole is a 16-sided bore whose flats are 0.2 mm outside the dowel (a 24-sided prism): a tip enters only within 1.2 mm of its hole's axis. Nothing is fixed, clamped or stopped.
scoring: Only the last step counts. Measured from the two boards' poses in the dowel board's frame: the gap between the ends at each corner of the seam (along the dowel board, negative if they overlap), the hole board's sideways offset and height step at its end, each board's tilt, and each dowel's tip depth in its own hole and distance off that hole's axis. Every rung needs: both corner gaps at least -0.5 mm, the height step within 1 mm, both boards within 3 deg of flat, and every dowel's tip at least 1 mm into its own hole within 1.2 mm of its axis (so stacked, overlapping or one-pitch-off boards score 0). 0.25: that. 0.5: and both corner gaps at most 10 mm. 0.75: seated: both corner gaps at most 0.3 mm and the edges flush within 0.3 mm. 0.9: seated, every pad point of both grippers at least 30 mm from both boards (and the dowels) and both boards under 5 mm/s. 1.0: that held 1 s (success). Nothing in the scene can break; no history is kept.
reset_notes: Dry fit, nothing consumed: pull the boards apart and set them on their taped outlines.
fidelity: Rigid boards and dowels with real contact. The sim's hole is 0.2 mm a side over the dowel, wider than the real 0 to 0.15 mm, as PhysX convex contacts jam in tighter fits; the dowels' flutes are not modelled and the fit has no dry-fit friction, so in the sim one arm can park its board and the other push on (in a real trial the press drags a free board). Entry capture and tilt binding are geometric.
scores: Dream-1 run: not run; demo: not run
